name: Congenital Contractural Arachnodactyly

criteria.description: Presence of long, slender fingers and toes (arachnodactyly)
Congenital contractures of large joints (elbows, knees, hips)
Characteristic crumpled or folded external ears
Identification of pathogenic FBN2 gene mutation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all three major criteria (arachnodactyly, congenital contractures, and crumpled ears) or identification of pathogenic FBN2 mutation with supportive clinical features
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing for FBN2 mutations can confirm diagnosis; differentiation from Marfan syndrome is critical.

imaging: Radiographs showing joint contractures and kyphoscoliosis
Echocardiography for mitral valve prolapse and aortic root assessment
other: Physical examination revealing crumpled ears and arachnodactyly
Family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance

distinguishingFeatures: Ectopia lentis common in Marfan but rare in congenital contractural arachnodactyly
Aortic root dilation more frequent and severe in Marfan syndrome
Absence of crumpled ears in Marfan syndrome
Multiple joint contractures present but without arachnodactyly or crumpled ears

redFlags: Severe progressive kyphoscoliosis causing respiratory compromise
Aortic root dilation with risk of dissection
Early onset joint contractures limiting mobility
references: Beals RK, Hecht F. Congenital contractural arachnodactyly. J Bone Joint Surg Am. 1971;53(7):1484-1491.
Faivre L, et al. Clinical and molecular study of congenital contractural arachnodactyly. Am J Med Genet A. 2007;143A(19):2280-2287.
commonPitfalls: Frequently misdiagnosed as Marfan syndrome due to overlapping skeletal features such as arachnodactyly and tall stature.
Mild contractures may be overlooked in infancy, leading to delayed diagnosis.
Crumpled ear helices, a key feature, are often missed on physical exam.
Joint hypermobility is less prominent than in Marfan syndrome, which can lead to confusion with other connective tissue disorders.

extendedDiscriminators.feature: Presence of congenital contractures (especially elbows, knees, fingers) and crumpled ear helices in congenital contractural arachnodactyly, which are not seen in Marfan syndrome.
Arachnodactyly and tall, thin habitus are characteristic of congenital contractural arachnodactyly but not typical of arthrogryposis multiplex congenita.
Ectopia lentis (lens dislocation) is common in Marfan syndrome but not seen in congenital contractural arachnodactyly.

ruleOutCriteria: Absence of congenital contractures of large joints (elbows, knees, fingers) essentially excludes congenital contractural arachnodactyly.
Presence of ectopia lentis (lens dislocation) strongly argues against congenital contractural arachnodactyly.
Lack of crumpled ear helices in a patient with otherwise suggestive features makes the diagnosis unlikely.
